content:
mike: quick check — I spotted TLS 1.2 handshakes to api.redwood-inference.com in the nginx access logs over the last 24h. I thought public LB was TLS1.3-only. Also: who owns rotation for Dedicated / Private certs (our KMS vs customer-managed)?

ana: we intended public LB to prefer 1.3. If 1.2 shows up it's likely an older client or a legacy edge. can you paste an example log line?

mike: sure, pasted below (sanitized):
```
2026-03-16T22:11:02Z nginx: "TLSv1.2 handshake" src=52.17.123.45 host=api.redwood-inference.com client_cipher=ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 cert_arn=arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:111222333:certificate/abc123
```

priya: that IP range looks like our on-prem backup agents in eu-west-1. infra-certops owns that fleet. for Dedicated certs we manage rotation via our infra KMS; for Private/VPC installs the customer can opt to bring their own keys (BYOK) — rotation there is customer-side unless we've been contracted to manage it.

ana: ok — two asks: 1) infra, can you add an LB rule to reject < TLS1.3 on the public endpoint and emit a metric/alert for rejected handshakes? 2) confirm no sensitive fields (full client IP or full cert ARNs) are being dumped to public S3 logs — we should hash/partial-redact before export.

priya: will do. we'll add a drop rule for TLS<1.3 behind a feature flag and emit a prometheus counter `lb.tls_reject_total{reason="legacy_tls"}`. will also add a pipeline step to redact IPs to `sha256(ip)` before moving logs to long-term S3. opening tickets: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-1987 (LB envoy rule) and https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/LOGS-342 (redaction pipeline).

sec-bot: Key rotation summary: last rotation completed 2026-02-10, next scheduled 2026-05-01, owner=infra-certops. Public LB currently configured to prefer TLS1.3 but will accept 1.2 for backward compatibility until the reject rule is deployed.

mike: thanks — I'll monitor INFRA-1987. one more: for Private deployments, who needs to sign off if we rotate a customer-provided cert on their behalf? legal/product?

ana: approvals needed = product + account manager + security. escalate to legal only if contract language requires preservation of the old key. for now, staged removal is fine — block 1.2 on public after infra patches the backup agents and redaction pipeline is in place. :thumbsup:

mike: great, filing follow-ups and pinging infra-certops. thx! :raised_hands:
